security.evidence: Strong core: entity-scoped findOrFail for every client-supplied id (Members.php:134,148,203,244), authorize() in mount and every mutating action, 403 on invite e-mail mismatch (PendingInvites.php:110), escaped Blade output and #[Fillable]. Gaps: selectedMembershipId (record id) and confirmingRemoval (flag) are client-writable without #[Locked] (Members.php:35,42), and closeMember()/cancelRemoval() do not authorize (Members.php:156-160,196-199). readability.evidence: Focused methods with clear names (openMember, saveRole, confirmRemoval, removeMember, inviteeInvite), docblocks explaining non-obvious decisions (Members.php:234-237) and comments on the race/idempotency paths (Members.php:108-109; PendingInvites.php:28,42,48). sendInvite() is long but linear and easy to follow.

scope.evidence: All edits serve the task: model/migration/factory/mail/lang/views/tests plus docs (CHANGELOG.md, docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md, docs/ops/logging.md). The Dashboard and default-page changes only hide the now manager-only members page, which is required by the task.

issues.explanation: selectedMembershipId and confirmingRemoval are public, client-writable record-id/flag properties without #[Locked], contrary to the mandatory Livewire policy; the id is re-resolved inside the entity and saveRole() authorizes it, so the impact is limited, but server-only state must be locked.

Input is validated with inline $this->validate([...]) instead of the project's #[Validate] (or rules()) plus $this->validate() pattern; validation is still server-side, but the project's standard for Livewire components is not followed.

closeMember() and cancelRemoval() are public Livewire endpoints that do not call $this->authorize(); they only mutate local UI state and the page mount is manager-gated, so impact is limited, but the Livewire rule is to authorize every action.

New domain writes (create/replace invite, create membership, update/delete membership) happen directly in the Livewire components instead of app/Actions/* as the project conventions require; this matches the old Members code but not the written domain-write rule.

The layout runs App\Models\EntityInvite::forEmail(...)->pending()->exists() inline in Blade on every page; this puts data access in a view and duplicates the pending-invites query that the PendingInvites component already owns.

decline() silently keeps an accepted invite, while the task says decline deletes the invite; the pending list never exposes accepted invites, so this is only reachable through a stale/tampered call, but it is a literal deviation.

The test named "creates a normalized invite, queues the mail and writes an audit log" never asserts the audit log (no Log::spy/shouldReceive), so the audit-log requirement is only verified by reading the implementation.

The members table now uses ui.name and ui.email, but the change adds only ui.role to lang/en/ui.php and lang/pt_BR/ui.php; confirm those two keys already exist in both locales, otherwise the headers render the raw keys.

review.summary: This is a functionally complete, well-tested implementation of invite-only membership: schema/model/factory, queued localized mail, pending-invite accept/decline, a manager-only members page with detail and removal modals, docs and a large Pest suite. It should not merge as is because it violates the project's mandatory Livewire policy: invite/role inputs use inline rules instead of #[Validate]/rules(), and the client-writable selectedMembershipId/confirmingRemoval are not #[Locked]; closeMember()/cancelRemoval() also lack an authorize call. The remaining findings (domain writes in the components, a Blade-side invite query, and a few nits) are minor once the policy items are fixed.
